llm.summary: The skill is coherent as VMware audit and policy infrastructure, but its documented fail-open and broad bypass behavior weakens safeguards for potentially destructive VMware operations.

dimensions.detail: The audit database records operation parameters, results, OS username, agent identity, workflow IDs, and risk level under ~/.vmware/audit.db, which is purpose-aligned but can retain sensitive infrastructure details and is easy to export in bulk.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation uses a uv package named vmware-policy and the artifact contains markdown only, with no executable scripts in the submitted files; however, it delegates runtime behavior to an external package not included in the artifact.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill is intended to auto-load for any VMware skill tool call, and the documentation describes policy enforcement that can be bypassed entirely with VMWARE_POLICY_DISABLED=1 and allows all operations when rules are absent or PyYAML is missing.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Persistent local audit storage and hot-reloaded policy rules are expected for this purpose, but the documented enforcement posture is fail-open and has an unrestricted environment-variable bypass across the VMware skill family.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose, audit logging, policy checks, sanitization, and CLI querying are coherent for shared VMware skill infrastructure, and the artifact says it exposes no MCP tools directly.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this before installing in production. It is not showing exfiltration or destructive behavior by itself, but policy enforcement is not fail-closed: operations may proceed if rules are not configured, if PyYAML is missing, or if VMWARE_POLICY_DISABLED=1 is set. Lock down ~/.vmware, configure rules.yaml deliberately, monitor any ok_bypassed entries, and handle audit exports as sensitive infrastructure data.
llm.findings:
[SQP-1] expected: Auto-loading for VMware tool calls is broad, but it matches the artifact's disclosed role as a shared decorator, audit, and policy layer rather than an unrelated hidden activation path.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The policy bypass, no-rules allow-all default, and PyYAML missing allow-all behavior are documented and materially weaken a policy-enforcement component used around high-impact VMware actions.
[SQP-2] expected: Local audit retention and JSON export are expected for compliance/audit functionality, but users should treat the records as sensitive because they may include operational metadata and results.
